summary: Let a viewer attempt to superimpose two mirror-image molecules and fail for a structural reason they can inspect.
objective: Build a pair of enantiomers I can rotate and translate freely to test whether they can be superimposed, with the four different substituents labelled.
intent_signals: Show why two mirror-image molecules are not the same molecule.
Let me try to line up a molecule with its mirror image.
example_prompts: Build an enantiomer pair I can rotate to test superimposition, with a mirror plane I can toggle.
Show a tetrahedral carbon with four different groups and its mirror image side by side.
negative_signals: Not a quantum chemistry, energy or optical rotation calculation.
Not a reaction mechanism or stereochemical nomenclature trainer.
not_for: Not a quantum chemistry, energy or optical rotation calculation.
Not a reaction mechanism or stereochemical nomenclature trainer.

entities.name: Molecule pair
entities.guidance: Two complete molecules built from the same substituent set with opposite handedness at the stereocenter, each independently transformable.

entities.name: Stereocenter marker
entities.guidance: Highlight the central atom and its four bonds with distinct substituent labels, since handedness is only meaningful when all four differ.

entities.name: Mirror reference
entities.guidance: Provide a toggleable mirror plane and a ghost image of the reflected molecule so the comparison is explicit rather than remembered.

state_contract.model: Two rigid molecules with independent orientation, a stereocenter with four labelled substituents, and a superimposition test that compares corresponding atom positions within a stated tolerance.
state_contract.authority: Atom identity and connectivity are authoritative; the superimposition verdict is computed from corresponding labelled atoms, never from a visual impression.
actions: Rotate and translate either molecule freely.
Run the superimposition test and read the residual mismatch.
Toggle the mirror plane and the reflected ghost.
Reset both molecules to their reference poses.

invariants: Rigid rotation and translation never change chirality; only reflection does.
The superimposition test reports failure with a residual value, not merely a verdict.
If two substituents are made identical the model must state that the centre is no longer a stereocenter.
motion_guidance: Animate rotation smoothly and let the viewer stop at any orientation; the failure to superimpose must remain inspectable at rest.
Do not snap the molecules into alignment as a reward; snapping would assert a false result.
known_limits: One stereocenter only; molecules with multiple centres, meso forms and conformational change are out of scope.
Bond lengths and angles are idealised for teaching, not optimised geometry.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: When a tetrahedral carbon carries four different substituents, the molecule and its mirror image cannot be brought into coincidence by rotation or translation, and the two forms are called enantiomers.
claims.scope: Single tetrahedral stereocentre only, independently paraphrased from the cited section. Molecules with several stereocentres, meso forms and other sources of chirality are outside this recipe.

object_craft.structure: Ball-and-stick construction with consistent atom radii and bond radii, plus a clearly modelled tetrahedral arrangement at the centre.
object_craft.material: Element-coded matte spheres with one reserved accent for the stereocenter; keep the two molecules identical in material so only geometry differs.
object_craft.articulation: Each molecule is a rigid transform group; substituents do not rotate independently in this recipe.

object_craft.structure: A bounded plane with a visible edge rather than an infinite sheet, plus a semi-transparent reflected ghost.
object_craft.material: Low-opacity ghost with a different surface treatment so it is never mistaken for a third molecule.
object_craft.articulation: The ghost is regenerated from the current pose of its source molecule.

physical_contract.scope: Rigid presentation transforms and a geometric comparison; no molecular dynamics or energetics.
checks: The superimposition test fails for the enantiomer pair at any orientation.
The same test succeeds when a molecule is compared with a rotated copy of itself.
